AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Controlling Soil Pollution? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Controlling Soil Pollution.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Controlling Soil Pollution.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Controlling Soil Pollution.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Controlling Soil Pollution.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparing Animal Products.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Preparing Animal Products.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparing Animal Products.

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Food Nutrients? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Food Nutrients.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Food Nutrients.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Food Nutrients.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Food Nutrients.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Constructing Water Retention Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Constructing Water Retention Structures.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Selected Crop Management Practises? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Selected Crop Management Practises.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Selected Crop Management Practises.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Selected Crop Management Practises.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Selected Crop Management Practises.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Trees? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Trees.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Trees.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Trees.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Trees.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene in Rearing Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene in Rearing Animals.

16. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
